subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Why Bridges Fail: Forces 101
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Why Bridges Fail: Forces 101.

hook.text: Every bridge on Earth is being pulled apart, crushed, and twisted at the same time.

buildup.text: Tension pulls things apart. Compression pushes them together. Bridges must handle both.

discovery.text: Steel is great in tension. Concrete is great in compression. Engineers use each where it excels.

twist.text: Wind adds a third force: torsion. It twists the bridge. That's what destroyed Tacoma Narrows.

climax.text: Bridge engineering is a constant battle against invisible forces trying to tear the structure apart.

punchline.text: A bridge is a negotiation with gravity.

quiz.question: What three main forces act on every bridge?
